note: Backend parity audit of the default surfaces. One row per capability and tool any maintained default declares; the maintained defaults are the default baseline's instances. tests/ora/agent/composition/surface/test_backend_parity.py checks that generic names are on every backend or excepted with a reason, that exceptions expire when the name is declared or the missing hook exists, that backend-specific names stay where they apply, and that a default swap keeps a superset of the default it replaced minus recorded retirements.

classes.generic: a Harness behaviour that applies on every backend; the agent code is backend-neutral
classes.generic_needs_backend_code: generic, but a backend may lack the implementation hook; an exception names the hook
classes.backend_specific: backend or embodiment identity, compiler, arm-count contract, backend-only mechanism or a tool shape another default legitimately lacks

exceptions.name: overhead_footprint_localization_v1
exceptions.reason: The overhead footprint localization became the LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro default on the evidence of a LIBERO-only paired screen; RoboTwin keeps the default its own results were measured on. The footprint centre is backend-neutral, but overhead_view_pose reads the single camera named wrist, so a dual-arm backend needs a per-arm camera choice and its own screen first.

exceptions.name: grasp_plan_ik_reachability_annotation_v1
exceptions.follow_up: a read-only IK reach route in each worker (RoboCasa: the robosuite IK probe behind a no-write RPC; RoboLab: a differential-IK solve on a cloned articulation), then declare the name
exceptions.reason: Proposed by the RoboCasa/RoboLab port and confirmed by the operator on 2026-10-18: neither backend serves a read-only IK reach route to the agent. RoboCasa's worker solves IK only inside its own move_pose admission (session.arm_path_plan) and RoboLab's absolute differential-IK action has no side-effect-free solve, so declaring the name would publish annotations the backend cannot compute.

exceptions.name: end_effector_speed_v1
exceptions.follow_up: RoboDojo: the toolkit default paces through the shared timing (shared_motion.py) and publishes speed in its own tools; only the frozen closed-skill surfaces leave their worker unpaced
exceptions.reason: User decision 2026-10-31: end-effector speed limiting and the wrist-unwind check become the default for every benchmark, LIBERO first. The pose tools send the speed in the motion action and LIBERO paces every route with ora/environment/controllers/motion_pace.py; this backend's executor does not read it yet, so declaring the name would publish a speed it ignores.
